phase: P12 (batch 1: customer care identity, roles and listings; module not registered in the API)
scope: customer-care routes (all 38), support ticket, chat session and feedback controllers, commands and services
all seven customer-care listing queries and their controllers
registration_decision: Not registered. The module has no customer-facing read routes (customers cannot see their own tickets or returns), so enabling it also needs a product decision on self-service.
reviewed_without_change: Agent management, goodwill creation and all deletes are admin-only.
Return item creation already checks that the order item belongs to the return's order (quantity limits are batch 2).

findings.file: support-ticket, chat-session and customer-feedback controllers; create-support-ticket and add-customer-feedback commands
findings.problem: The public ticket, chat and feedback routes (anonymous allowed) created records under the userId in the request body, so anyone could open tickets, chats or feedback as any customer.
findings.change: Records are created for the signed-in user; only customer care staff may create them for a named customer.
findings.verification: Reviewed with the controllers; the service-level rules below are unit tested.

findings.problem: Tickets could reference any order, and feedback ownership checks were fail-open: skipped without a body userId, skipped when the lookups were not wired, and guest orders accepted for anyone.
findings.change: One fail-closed rule: customers may reference only their own orders and tickets, anonymous callers none, staff any; a missing lookup refuses.
findings.verification: Unit customer-care-access: baseline 8 of 11 cases failed (all refusals accepted); fixed refusals hold and owner, staff and order-less tickets still work.

findings.problem: Seven write routes (ticket updates and messages, ending chats and chat messages, creating returns, return items and repairs) allowed every staff role, including the read-only ANALYST and INVENTORY_STAFF roles.
findings.change: These writes require ADMIN or CUSTOMER_SERVICE; reads remain staff-level.

findings.file: seven list-*.query.ts handlers and their controllers; application/queries/paging.ts
findings.problem: Every customer-care listing ignored its query and loaded the whole table (no default limit in the repositories).
findings.change: Listings are always paged: 50 per page by default, at most 100, with limit/offset taken from the request.
findings.verification: Unit list-paging: bounds cases and the handler case; baseline the handler called the service with no limit.

tests.baseline: customer-care-access 8 of 11 failed (the 3 allowed cases passed by design); list-paging handler case failed.
tests.database_suites: Not rerun for this batch: no registered code changed (module not wired into the API); last full run 167 tests in 48 files at 2d47a2ac. Rerun with batch 2.
tests.final: 1544 unit tests in 121 files; root/tooling tsc; 7/7 workspace type-checks; customer-care ESLint (no errors)

follow_ups: Owner decision on registering the module and on customer self-service routes.
Return integrity (status transitions, quantity limits, Prisma order port) is P12 batch 2.
Controllers use their own response envelope and untyped route handlers (as any).
